text.p: Algeria's government-appointed human rights leader said on Tuesday the country, which has been criticised for human rights abuses, had a "satisfactory" level in protecting and promoting such rights.
The official Algerian news agency APS quoted Rezzag Bara as saying Algeria had acquired "a level comparable to all other countries who have ratified the conventions and agreements on human rights."

Bara heads the National Observatory of Human Rights, an officially appointed body in the North African country in which security forces have been fighting Moslem fundamentalist rebels for the past five years. About 60,000 people have been killed.
Last month, the London-based rights group Amnesty International said there was widescale abuses in human rights and that "an atmosphere of terror and lawlessness" ruled in Algeria.
Algeria then accused Amnesty International of bias and said it persisted in "equating law enforcement forces with terrorist groups, whom it sees as an armed opposition".
